Subject: Post-call recap — connection gating, streaming & quota ask

Sam — thanks for the time this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment going into engineering review.

Call highlights:
- BrightEdge target SLOs: 99th pctl tail latency <= 200ms for short text responses (<=128 tokens), avg latency target ~80–120ms.
- Expected steady-state throughput: ~1,200 requests/sec across the integration.
- Concurrency profile: ~180 long-lived concurrent streaming requests (SSE/chunked responses) during peak, with short lived spikes up to 400 parallel requests for short bursts (~2–5 minutes).
- Streaming: chunked HTTP streaming to support incremental tokens for inference (server → client). You mentioned needing low time-to-first-byte for partial tokens.
- Connection behavior: pref HTTP/2 multiplexing from a small fleet of backend hosts; want persistent connections + connection pooling in our client.

Open items we agreed to investigate:
1) Redwood hosted default rate limits and how those translate to per-connection multiplexing and 429 behavior.
2) Proposal for a negotiated quota (sustained qps + burst window + concurrency cap) or Dedicated pool recommendation.
3) Any SDK-level guidance for keeping latency low with streaming + KV cache considerations.

Attached: BrightEdge action plan template (sheet) — fill in your exact traffic pattern and we'll turn it into a capacity proposal.

Proposed next steps:
- I'm going to loop in Solutions (Marissa) to produce a capacity/burst proposal by EOD Tue.
- Marissa will propose a technical configuration (connection limits, recommended multiplexing, cache advice).
- If the numbers line up, we can spin a short dedicated canary pool for a 2-week soak.

If any of the numbers above are off, flag them in a reply and we'll adjust.

Thanks,
Jordan Blake
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Hi Sam — looped in per Jordan. Quick technical notes while we build the capacity proposal:

1) HTTP/2 & multiplexing: Redwood supports HTTP/2 multiplexing on the hosted API — clients can maintain a small number of persistent connections and multiplex multiple streams. Hosted defaults are conservative to protect noisy neighbors; for production traffic we recommend a negotiated quota or Dedicated pool which removes many of those limits.

2) Default behavior on limits: hosted endpoints will return 429 with Retry-After headers for rate limits; for connection-level resource constraints you can see transient 503s. For predictable customer-grade behaviour (no 429s under steady load) we recommend either a negotiated production quota (hosted, higher limits + rate limit reservations) or Dedicated (reserved capacity + SLA).

3) Suggested baseline for BrightEdge (proposal draft):
- Sustained: 2,000 rps across region(s)
- Burst: 6,000 rps for up to 5 minutes (burst window configurable)
- Concurrency (streaming long-lived): reserved capacity for 300 parallel streams (safe headroom on your 250 estimate)
- Per-connection guidance: maintain 6–8 HTTP/2 connections from each origin host and multiplex within them; keep-alive enabled; limit simultaneous outstanding requests per connection to ~50 to avoid head-of-line effects.

4) Performance considerations: short responses (<=128 tokens) are dominated by scheduling and kernel latency; ensure you pin model to a lower-latency variant (we'll recommend a quantized instance for production). We also recommend prefix caching for common prompts which reduces repeated compute.

5) Next steps I will deliver by Tue: a one-page capacity table (sustained/burst/concurrency), an initial ratecard estimate (attached PDF outline), and a checklist for SDK-level retry/backoff + circuit-breaker settings.

Marissa
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
